title: Default lot
description:
Distribuția programelor SRTV prin satelit va fi următoarea (listă de regiuni de distribuție):
a.	În România și Republica Moldova precum şi la sediile ambasadelor României din Europa din Egipt și din Israel
b.	Europa, pe unul dintre sateliții Hotbird13°E sau Astra19.2°E: TVR INTERNAȚIONAL 
c.	În America de Nord (Statele Unite ale Americii și Canada): TVR INTERNAȚIONAL 
d.	În Australia și Noua Zeelandă: TVR INTERNAȚIONAL 
Pentru distribuţia în zona „a” (Pachetul SRTv pentru România si Europa) distribuţie primară se va oferta un trasponder în banda Ku (complet, în saturaţie) , în bandă Ku, pe acelaşi satelit şi cu acceaşi polaritate pentru distribuţia programelor SRTv.
Pe satelitul ofertat trebuie să existe un DTH românesc şi să existe şi alte canale ale televiziunilor din România
Soluția de satelit propusă de ofertant trebuie să asigure faptul că programele TVR vor putea fi recepționate cu antenă parabolică de 90 cm în banda Ku și receptoare DVB-S2.
Pentru celelalte regiuni („b”, „c” şi „d”) în care se va distribui doar TVR INTERNAŢIONAL ofertantul va propune un canal de 3 MHz într-o platformă de tip DTH.
Satelitul propus trebuie să facă parte dintr-o flotă de sateliți a ofertantului care acesta le deţine în administraţie trebuie să facă dovada prin angajamente contractuale că, în cazul în care satelitul/transpondereIe se defectează, în termen de maximum 24 de ore, poate realoca emisia TVR pe un alt satelit/transponder de pe una dintre pozițiile orbitale pe care societățile de distribuție prin cablu din România au deja instalate antene de receptie. Aceste poziții orbitală sunt următoarele: 1°W, 16°E, 39°E. Toate condiţiile de mai sus vor fi obligaţii stipulate în contract.
Ofertantul trebuie să facă dovada că deţine în administrare sau chiar în proprietate a minim 3 sateliţi şi trei sateliţi de rezervă simultani care pot prelua semanlul din zonele „b”, „c”, şi „d” astfel încât transmisia să fie continuă
Cantitatea minima acord cadru - 1 luna
Cantitate maxima acord cadru - 48 luni
Cel mai mic contract subsecvent - 1 luna
Cel mai mare contract subsecvent - 12 luni
Se vor incheia un numar de 16 contracte subsecvent in cadrul acordului cadru

title: Airborne Camera System for Stereo Mapping and Orthophoto Production
description:
The National Land Survey of Finland (NLS) is acquiring one (1) airborne camera system for stereo mapping and orthophoto production, all the software and hardware which are needed to operate the airborne camera system, image processing software, and documentation (hereinafter "Product"). Product is specified in more detail in Appendices 1a "Description of the procurement" and 1b "Mandatory requirements". 

The procurement also covers the following services:
- delivery of the Product
- guidance and assistance in installation of the Product to the National Land Survey of Finland's airplane
- geometric and radiometric calibration of the Product
- basic and advanced training
- maintenance services for the Product according to Clause 21 of Appendix A "Contract" and Appendix 1c "Requirements for maintenance".

CONTRACT PERIOD

The Contract (Appendix A) comes into force on the date of signing of the Contract. The delivery schedule for the Product is specified in Clause 9 of the Contract. The Contract is in force until all obligations under it have been fulfilled.

The supplier shall provide the maintenance services according to Appendix 1c "Requirements for maintenance" for a fixed period of 7 years. After the fixed period the supplier shall provide the maintenance services according to Appendix 1c until further notice. The 7-year fixed period includes the warranty period.

OPTION

During the contract period of the maintenance services, the NLS has an option to upgrade the camera system components to newer, improved versions. Such components may include a solution to prevent GNSS interference (e.g. jamming). The content and price of the upgrade will be agreed separately between the NLS and the supplier. The terms of the Contract and the Appendix 1c "Requirements for maintenance" shall apply to the upgrade as applicable.

title: SPACE4Cities Pre-Commercial Procurement Call for Tenders on "Opening European satellite data for city planning"
description:
SPACE4Cities Pre-Commercial Procurement Call for Tenders on "Opening European satellite data for city planning". 
This PCP procurement is a joint procurement by different procurers across Europe that are all facing the same common challenge and are thus looking for similar solutions (so-called ‘buyers group’). The procurement will take the form of a pre-commercial procurement (PCP) under which R&D service contracts will be awarded to a number of R&D providers (Suppliers)  in parallel in a phased approach. This will make it possible to compare competing alternative solutions. Each selected R&D provider will be awarded a framework agreement that covers the following R&D phases and a specific contract per phase (if indeed selected for the next phase). 
The 3 phases are: solution design (phase 1 with 20 selected Suppliers), prototyping and lab testing (phase 2 with 10 Suppliers), original development, installation, validation and field testing of a limited set of first products or services (phase 3 with 5 Suppliers).
After each phase, intermediate evaluations will be carried out to progressively select the best of the competing solutions. The contractors with the best evaluation scores (based on the functional and non-functional requirements in Tender Document 2) will be offered a specific contract for the next phase. Testing in Phase 3 is expected to take place in Helsinki, Amsterdam, Ghent, Guimaraes and the Attica Region, as well as 10 (smaller) tests in yet-to-be-defined cities throughout Europe. This testing may also serve as a first customer test reference for the contractors. 
The procurement is expected to start in May 2025 (after selection of the Phase 1 Suppliers) and end in April 2027. 
The selected operators will retain ownership of the intellectual property rights (IPRs) that they generate during the PCP and will be able to use them to exploit the full market potential of the developed solutions i.e. beyond the procurers. The market potential is estimated to be large.

title: SPACE4Cities Pre-Commercial Procurement Call for Tenders on "Opening European satellite data for city planning"
description:
SPACE4Cities Pre-Commercial Procurement Call for Tenders on "Opening European satellite data for city planning". 
This PCP procurement is a joint procurement by different procurers across Europe that are all facing the same common challenge and are thus looking for similar solutions (so-called ‘buyers group’). The procurement will take the form of a pre-commercial procurement (PCP) under which R&D service contracts will be awarded to a number of R&D providers (Suppliers)  in parallel in a phased approach. This will make it possible to compare competing alternative solutions. Each selected R&D provider will be awarded a framework agreement that covers the following R&D phases and a specific contract per phase (if indeed selected for the next phase). 
The 3 phases are: solution design (phase 1 with 20 selected Suppliers), prototyping and lab testing (phase 2 with 10 Suppliers), original development, installation, validation and field testing of a limited set of first products or services (phase 3 with 5 Suppliers).
After each phase, intermediate evaluations will be carried out to progressively select the best of the competing solutions. The contractors with the best evaluation scores (based on the functional and non-functional requirements in Tender Document 2) will be offered a specific contract for the next phase. Testing in Phase 3 is expected to take place in Helsinki, Amsterdam, Ghent, Guimaraes and the Attica Region, as well as 10 (smaller) tests in yet-to-be-defined cities throughout Europe. This testing may also serve as a first customer test reference for the contractors. 
The procurement is expected to start in May 2025 (after selection of the Phase 1 Suppliers) and end in April 2027. 
The selected operators will retain ownership of the intellectual property rights (IPRs) that they generate during the PCP and will be able to use them to exploit the full market potential of the developed solutions i.e. beyond the procurers. The market potential is estimated to be large.
